content.title: About
content.content: Plain whole‑milk yogurt is made by fermenting whole cow’s milk with live cultures of Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus. It has a creamy texture, mild milky flavor, and contains about 3.5 % fat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Yogurt originated in Mesopotamia over 5,000 years ago, with the modern fermentation method documented in Turkey.
Live cultures in yogurt can support a healthy gut microbiome.
Whole milk gives the yogurt a richer taste and higher levels of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).
In many cultures yogurt is traditionally served with honey, nuts, or fresh berries.
Yogurt is often used as a base for sauces, marinades, and desserts.

items.title: Rich in probiotics
items.content: Live bacteria help maintain gut microbial balance, supporting digestion and immunity.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Whole‑milk yogurt provides calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is important for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Approximately 4 g of protein per 100 g helps promote satiety and tissue repair.

items.title: Fat‑soluble vitamins
items.content: The fat in whole milk aids absorption of vitamins A, D, E, and K.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming yogurt.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey protein requires complete avoidance of the product.

items.title: Fat content
items.content: Whole‑milk yogurt contains about 3.5 % fat, which should be considered by those monitoring fat intake.

items.title: Natural sugar
items.content: Unsweetened versions contain lactose, a natural milk sugar, but no added sugars.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Yogurt can be enjoyed on its own, blended into smoothies, used in sauces, dressings, casseroles, and desserts. It pairs well with berries, honey, nuts, or granola.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store yogurt in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
